questions.q: A 35-year-old male presents with multiple hypopigmented macules over the trunk with loss of sensation. Slit-skin smear shows solid-staining bacilli in large numbers (BI 5+). Which of the following best describes his leprosy classification per Ridley-Jopling?
questions.exp: Lepromatous leprosy (LL) shows high bacterial index (BI 4-6+) due to absent cell-mediated immunity, with numerous solid-staining bacilli (globi) on smear. Multiple hypopigmented macules with loss of sensation and high BI is classical LL.

questions.q: A 28-year-old HIV-positive patient develops painful grouped vesicles on an erythematous base along the right T5 dermatome. The most appropriate antiviral and its dosage for this immunocompromised patient is:
questions.exp: Herpes zoster in immunocompromised patients requires high-dose acyclovir 800 mg 5 times/day for 7–10 days to reduce viral load and prevent dissemination. Valacyclovir 1 g TDS is also acceptable but acyclovir 800 mg 5×/day is the standard first-line.

questions.q: A 22-year-old woman presents with tense bullae on normal and erythematous skin, predominantly over the flexures. Direct immunofluorescence (DIF) shows linear IgG and C3 deposits at the basement membrane zone. The target antigen is most likely:
questions.exp: Bullous pemphigoid (BP) targets BP180 (collagen XVII, BPAG2) and BP230 (BPAG1). DIF shows linear IgG/C3 at BMZ. Tense flexural bullae on normal/erythematous skin is classic for BP. Type VII collagen is targeted in epidermolysis bullosa acquisita.

questions.q: A 45-year-old male with a 10-year history of psoriasis develops swollen, painful joints with telescoping of fingers and 'pencil-in-cup' deformity on X-ray. Which type of psoriatic arthritis does he have?
questions.exp: Arthritis mutilans is the most severe (5% of psoriatic arthritis cases) characterised by osteolysis, telescoping ('opera-glass' or 'main en lorgnette') deformity, and 'pencil-in-cup' appearance on X-ray due to resorption of bone ends.

questions.q: A 30-year-old woman presents with a 6-month history of erythematous, itchy, vesicular eruption on the elbows, knees, and buttocks. Biopsy from perilesional skin shows IgA deposits at the tips of dermal papillae. The most likely underlying association is:
questions.exp: Dermatitis herpetiformis (DH) is strongly associated with coeliac disease (gluten-sensitive enteropathy). DIF shows granular IgA at the tips of dermal papillae. Treatment involves a gluten-free diet and dapsone.

questions.q: A 25-year-old uncircumcised male presents with a painless indurated ulcer on the glans penis for 2 weeks. Non-treponemal tests (VDRL) are negative. The next best step in diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Primary chancre of syphilis presents 9–90 days post-exposure as a painless indurated genital ulcer. VDRL/RPR may be seronegative in early primary syphilis. Dark-field microscopy of fresh exudate is the gold standard for direct detection of T. pallidum spirochaetes.

questions.q: A 40-year-old female is diagnosed with systemic lupus erythematosus. She develops a photosensitive rash and her ANA is positive in a homogeneous pattern. Which autoantibody is most specific for SLE and correlates with disease activity and lupus nephritis?
questions.exp: Anti-dsDNA antibody is highly specific for SLE (~97%) and titres correlate with disease activity, particularly lupus nephritis. Anti-Smith is most specific but does not correlate with activity. Anti-Ro/La are seen in subacute cutaneous LE and neonatal lupus.

questions.q: A 50-year-old farmer presents with a verrucous nodule on the dorsum of the right hand for 8 months. Biopsy shows pseudoepitheliomatous hyperplasia, suppurative granulomas, and medlar bodies (sclerotic bodies). The causative organism is:
questions.exp: Chromoblastomycosis is caused by dematiaceous (pigmented) fungi such as Fonsecaea pedrosoi, Cladophialophora carrionii, and Phialophora verrucosa. Pathognomonic finding is muriform cells (sclerotic/medlar bodies) — brown, round, thick-walled bodies dividing by septation.

questions.q: A 3-year-old boy presents with honey-coloured crusted lesions around the nose and mouth. Gram stain of crust reveals Gram-positive cocci in clusters. The most common causative organism and its toxin responsible for this condition are:
opts: Staphylococcus aureus; toxic shock syndrome toxin-1
questions.exp: Non-bullous impetigo is most commonly caused by Staphylococcus aureus (sometimes S. pyogenes). The exfoliative toxin (ET-A, ET-B) produced by S. aureus phage group II cleaves desmoglein 1, causing the superficial blistering and honey-coloured crusting.

questions.q: A 60-year-old male presents with a pearly, translucent nodule with rolled edges and telangiectasia on the nasolabial fold. Biopsy shows basaloid cells with peripheral palisading and artefactual clefting. The most appropriate surgical margin for low-risk basal cell carcinoma is:
questions.exp: For low-risk BCC (nodular, well-defined, < 2 cm, primary, non-high-risk site), standard excision with 3–4 mm margins achieves > 95% clearance rate. High-risk or recurrent BCC warrants Mohs micrographic surgery.

questions.q: A 19-year-old male presents with multiple comedones, papules, and nodulo-cystic lesions over the face and trunk for 3 years, unresponsive to antibiotics and topical retinoids. The most important pre-treatment investigation before starting oral isotretinoin is:
opts: Liver function tests and serum triglycerides
questions.exp: Before starting isotretinoin, baseline LFTs and fasting lipids (triglycerides, cholesterol) are mandatory since the drug can cause hepatotoxicity and hypertriglyceridemia. A pregnancy test (urine/serum beta-hCG) is essential in females of childbearing potential due to teratogenicity.

questions.q: A 32-year-old woman develops painful oral erosions, flaccid bullae, and Nikolsky sign positivity. DIF shows intercellular IgG deposits in a 'chicken-wire' or 'fishnet' pattern throughout the epidermis. The target antigen is:
questions.exp: Pemphigus vulgaris predominantly targets Desmoglein 3 (mucosal involvement) and in more extensive disease, both Dsg3 and Dsg1. Mucosal-dominant PV targets Dsg3; muco-cutaneous PV targets both. DIF reveals intercellular IgG in a fishnet/chicken-wire pattern.

questions.q: A 38-year-old male with occupational exposure to chromium salts presents with a painless chronic ulcer on the dorsum of the right forearm with heaped-up margins. Histology shows well-differentiated squamous cell carcinoma. The node-positive staging (N1) in the AJCC 8th edition staging for cutaneous SCC corresponds to:
opts: Single ipsilateral lymph node > 3 cm but ≤ 6 cm
questions.exp: Per AJCC 8th edition for cutaneous SCC: N1 = single ipsilateral lymph node ≤ 3 cm in greatest dimension without extranodal extension; N2a = single ipsilateral node > 3–6 cm; N2b = multiple ipsilateral nodes ≤ 6 cm; N3 = > 6 cm or ENE.

questions.q: A 24-year-old female presents with irregular patches of hypopigmentation over the face with fine scaling. Wood's lamp examination shows minimal enhancement. KOH mount from scale shows 'spaghetti and meatballs' appearance. The drug of choice for extensive disease is:
questions.exp: Pityriasis versicolor due to Malassezia furfur shows hyphae and yeast cells ('spaghetti and meatballs') on KOH. For extensive disease, oral itraconazole 200 mg/day × 7 days or 200 mg/day × 5 days is effective. Ketoconazole is now less preferred due to hepatotoxicity concerns.

questions.q: A 55-year-old male with rheumatoid arthritis on long-term hydroxychloroquine presents with difficulty reading and colour vision abnormality. The type of toxicity and the earliest finding on investigations is:
opts: Retinal toxicity; bull's-eye maculopathy on fundoscopy
Retinal toxicity; ring scotoma on automated perimetry
questions.exp: Hydroxychloroquine retinal toxicity presents initially as a paracentral scotoma (ring scotoma) detectable on automated visual field testing (Humphrey perimetry 10-2 pattern) before the classic bull's-eye maculopathy on fundoscopy appears. Baseline eye exam and annual screening are recommended.

questions.q: A 42-year-old man presents with fever, arthralgia, and a purpuric non-blanching rash over the lower limbs. Skin biopsy shows leucocytoclastic vasculitis with neutrophil infiltration around small vessels and nuclear dust. Immunofluorescence reveals IgA deposits. The most likely diagnosis is:
questions.exp: IgA vasculitis (Henoch-Schönlein purpura) is characterised by IgA immune deposits in small vessel walls. Classic tetrad: palpable purpura (lower limbs), arthritis, abdominal pain, renal involvement. DIF shows IgA deposits in vessel walls.

questions.q: During a Mohs micrographic surgery procedure, the tissue is processed and examined. Which of the following correctly describes the difference between Mohs surgery and standard excision histology?
opts: Mohs uses vertical sectioning examining 100% of margins; standard excision uses bread-loaf vertical sections examining < 1% of margins
Mohs uses bread-loaf vertical sections; standard excision uses horizontal frozen sections
Both techniques examine 100% of surgical margins
Mohs uses permanent sections; standard uses frozen sections
questions.exp: Mohs micrographic surgery uses horizontal (en-face) frozen sections of the entire undersurface and peripheral margins, examining nearly 100% of the surgical margin. Traditional bread-loaf vertical sectioning of a standard excision specimen examines < 1–2% of the true margin, missing potential residual tumour.

questions.q: A 16-year-old boy presents with diffuse hyperpigmentation of the face, axillae, and groin with velvety, papillomatous thickening. His BMI is 38 kg/m². The most important investigation to order given his presentation is:
opts: Fasting blood glucose and insulin levels
questions.exp: Acanthosis nigricans in an obese adolescent is most likely benign/obesity-associated and linked to insulin resistance. Fasting glucose and insulin levels (with HOMA-IR) are essential to screen for type 2 diabetes and metabolic syndrome. Malignant AN (seen in adults with rapid onset) requires workup for internal malignancy.

questions.q: A 70-year-old female with a long history of chronic venous insufficiency develops a large, slow-growing verrucous plaque on the lower leg, initially resembling a wart. Biopsy reveals well-differentiated SCC with pushing margins, minimal cytological atypia, and extensive keratinization. This is best classified as:
questions.exp: Verrucous carcinoma is a low-grade, well-differentiated variant of SCC with three main types: oral (Ackerman tumour), anogenital (giant condyloma Buschke-Löwenstein), and plantar (epithelioma cuniculatum). It shows pushing (not infiltrating) deep margins, minimal atypia, and rare metastasis. Chronic lymphoedema/venous stasis is a risk factor.

questions.q: A 28-year-old female who is 12 weeks pregnant develops widespread erythema and erosions starting in the periumbilical area. DIF shows linear C3 ± IgG along the BMZ. The drug of choice for this condition during pregnancy is:
questions.exp: Pemphigoid gestationis (herpes gestationis) is an autoimmune bullous disease of pregnancy targeting BP180 (collagen XVII). DIF shows linear C3 ± IgG at BMZ. Oral prednisolone (systemic corticosteroids) is the treatment of choice. MMF is contraindicated in pregnancy (teratogenic); dapsone should be avoided near term.

questions.q: A 35-year-old male from Maharashtra presents with indurated painless swelling of the scrotum and feet with multiple sinuses discharging pale yellowish-white granules. X-ray shows bony destruction. The most common causative organism in India for this condition is:
questions.exp: Mycetoma (Madura foot) presents with the classic triad of painless swelling, sinuses, and discharge of granules. In India, the most common causative agent is Madurella mycetomatis (eumycetoma, black grains), followed by Actinomadura madurae (actinomycetoma, white/pale grains). Madurella mycetomatis predominates in India.

questions.q: A 45-year-old female presents with Raynaud's phenomenon, sclerodactyly, telangiectasias, and dysphagia. Her ANA pattern is centromeric. She does NOT have pulmonary fibrosis. The most likely diagnosis and its associated risk of pulmonary hypertension (PAH) is:
opts: Diffuse systemic sclerosis; low risk of PAH
Limited systemic sclerosis (CREST); high risk of PAH
Mixed connective tissue disease; low risk of PAH
questions.exp: CREST syndrome (Calcinosis, Raynaud's, Esophageal dysmotility, Sclerodactyly, Telangiectasia) = limited systemic sclerosis. Anti-centromere antibody (ACA) is the hallmark. Limited SSc has high risk of isolated pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) but lower risk of interstitial lung disease compared to diffuse SSc.

questions.q: Nikolsky sign is positive in all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Nikolsky sign (lateral pressure on normal skin causes epidermal sliding/separation) is positive in conditions with intraepidermal blistering or superficial epidermal detachment: pemphigus vulgaris, SSSS, TEN/SJS. It is classically NEGATIVE in bullous pemphigoid (subepidermal blistering), though Asboe-Hansen sign may be positive.

questions.q: A 20-year-old male presents with grouped papules, pustules, and comedones in the beard area following shaving. Culture grows Staphylococcus aureus. The term for this condition and the recommended topical treatment is:
opts: Sycosis barbae; topical mupirocin or fusidic acid
questions.exp: Sycosis barbae is a chronic staphylococcal folliculitis of the bearded area. Topical mupirocin or fusidic acid are effective first-line treatments for mild-moderate disease. Tinea barbae is a fungal folliculitis (dermatophyte). Pseudofolliculitis is an ingrown hair problem common in curly-haired individuals.

questions.q: A 25-year-old female sex worker presents with a painless genital ulcer with indurated margins for 3 weeks. She is tested and found VDRL reactive at 1:32. To confirm the diagnosis, the most specific treponemal test is:
questions.exp: FTA-ABS is the most specific treponemal test and becomes positive earliest in syphilis (even before VDRL). TPHA is also treponemal and specific. Non-treponemal tests (VDRL, RPR) are sensitive but non-specific (false positives in SLE, pregnancy, malaria, etc.). FTA-ABS remains positive lifelong even after treatment.

questions.q: A 55-year-old male presents with a well-demarcated, annular, scaly plaque on the scalp with broken hair stumps. KOH mount shows arthroconidia arranged in a mosaic pattern outside the hair shaft. The type of invasion and the most likely causative organism are:
questions.exp: Ectothrix dermatophyte invasion = arthroconidia in a mosaic pattern OUTSIDE the hair shaft; caused by Microsporum species (M. canis, M. audouinii, M. gypseum) and T. verrucosum. Endothrix (spores inside hair shaft) is caused by T. tonsurans, T. violaceum. M. canis fluoresces green under Wood's lamp.

questions.q: A 10-year-old child presents with a verrucous, warty plaque with satellite lesions on the right hand. The dermoscopy shows a 'mosaic' pattern of papillary loops. The child's parents ask about cryotherapy. The appropriate freeze-thaw cycle for common warts is:
opts: Double freeze-thaw cycle with each freeze of 10–30 seconds
Triple freeze-thaw cycle for 60 seconds each
Single freeze for 60 seconds without thaw
questions.exp: Standard cryotherapy for common warts uses a double freeze-thaw cycle. Each freeze lasts 10–30 seconds (until a 1–2 mm ice ball forms beyond the lesion), followed by complete thaw. Double freeze-thaw is more effective than single cycle for viral warts.

questions.q: A 30-year-old man presents with erythematous plaques with silvery scales over the extensor surfaces and scalp. A 'candle-grease sign,' 'Auspitz sign,' and 'Koebner phenomenon' are noted. Which of the following biologic agents targets the p40 subunit shared by IL-12 and IL-23?
questions.exp: Ustekinumab is a monoclonal antibody targeting the p40 subunit shared by IL-12 and IL-23, blocking both Th1 and Th17 pathways. Secukinumab and ixekizumab target IL-17A; guselkumab targets the p19 subunit of IL-23 specifically.

questions.q: A 65-year-old male presents with a single indurated plaque on the right cheek with central keratotic plug. Dermoscopy shows a 'white circle' surrounding a central keratin mass with peripheral vessels. Histology reveals a crater-like lesion filled with keratin, surrounded by well-differentiated squamous epithelium. The correct management is:
opts: Excision with 5 mm margins to exclude SCC
questions.exp: Keratoacanthoma (KA) may spontaneously involute but is histologically indistinguishable from well-differentiated SCC in many cases. Current consensus favours excision (not just observation) to achieve definitive diagnosis and treatment. Excision with adequate margins is preferred over destructive methods that destroy tissue.

questions.q: A 40-year-old woman presents with symmetrical hyperpigmented patches over the malar area and forehead that worsen in summer. She is on oral contraceptive pills. The modified Kligman's formula (triple combination) used for treatment contains:
questions.exp: The modified Kligman's formula (triple combination) for melasma contains: Hydroquinone 4% (depigmenting) + Tretinoin 0.05% (retinoid, enhances penetration and turnover) + Fluocinolone acetonide 0.01% (low-potency steroid, reduces irritation). The original Kligman's used dexamethasone; fluocinolone acetonide replaced it in the modified version.
